body.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), suppose \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) is fixed, the primitive conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\) hold along the base law and contiguous joint-chart paths, and \(\sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1)\). Then \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},\] \(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and \(P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\). The contiguous-path expansion makes the estimator regular and efficient for the observed joint-bridge functional.
body.justification: The theorem converts the conditional quotient gradient into regular pointwise inference under explicit approximation, estimation, conditioning, envelope, ridge, and mixed-bias rates.
body.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already gives root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear and locally efficient selected-representative inference under additional regularity; BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified gives selected-limit inference, and AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE gives uniquely indexed GMM. None learns the global affine score projection across two nonunique bridge fibers.
body.consumer: A SUPPORT reanalysis can report a variance-minimizing affine-ensemble standard error together with the selected-pair benchmark.

obligation.what_is_open: Asymptotic linearity of the explicit learned affine ensemble, and hence its ratio-consistent variance, Wald coverage, regularity, and efficiency.
obligation.obstruction: The theorem requires the unresolved learned-projection convergence lemma. In addition, the phrase that primitive conditions hold along contiguous paths does not specify the uniform local envelopes needed to prove regularity. The general canonical-gradient premise also fails outside a path-rich chart.
obligation.attempted: Derived the exact conditional mixed-bias identity and the cross-fit empirical-process reduction; the remaining first-order signal convergence is precisely the unproved learned-projection step.
obligation.partial_result:
If the unresolved learned-signal step were established so that, foldwise,
\(\|\widehat\psi-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2=o_p(1)\), then training/holdout independence would give
\[
 \sqrt n(\mathbb P_n-P)\{\widehat\psi-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\}=o_p(1).
\]
Together with the proved mixed-bias bound and
\(\sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1)\), this would imply
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).
\]
For \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), the i.i.d. central limit theorem and the same \(L^2\) convergence then yield pointwise normality, \(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and Wald coverage.  The antecedent is not derivable from the current primitive assumptions because \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\) is not established; regularity under contiguous paths additionally requires a precise uniform local version of these rates.
